definition: How consistently a method gives the same results when it is repeated under the same conditions; a reliable method is not necessarily valid, because it can consistently measure the wrong thing.
Whether a method measures what it claims to measure, so that its results and conclusions are accurate.
A reliability check in which the same group takes the same test at two different times; a strong positive correlation between the two sets of scores suggests the test is reliable.
A reliability check in which the same group takes two equivalent versions of a test; a strong positive correlation between the two sets of scores suggests the test is reliable.
The extent to which a test covers every part of what it is meant to measure, in sensible proportions.
The extent to which a test's results agree with an established measure of the same thing (the criterion); a strong correlation in the expected direction between the two suggests the test is valid.
